title: Decolonial AI Alignment: Openness, Viśeṣa-Dharma, and Including Excluded Knowledges
benchmark_measurement: The paper critiques the 'moral absolutism' in current LLM alignment practices, which erases non-Western moral philosophies, and proposes a decolonial framework based on Hindu concepts like dharma and viśeṣa-dharma. It does not empirically measure model performance on religious tasks.
findings: The paper argues that current LLM alignment practices are colonial due to their 'moral absolutism,' which centers Western, universalist moral philosophies. It proposes that the moral philosophy of Hinduism, particularly the concepts of an open-source tradition and viśeṣa-dharma (context-specific right/wrong), offers a superior framework for a decolonial AI alignment. This dharmic approach would empower communities to align models to their own contextual values using open models and accessible technologies like LoRA, and would accept diverse epistemologies where values are expressed through stories and other forms, not just explicit commandments.
